title: Decision models for data scientists: one answer about a column, the same through the API, the MCP tool and the companion
request: The technical decision points as something a data scientist asks while working: an API, an MCP tool, the notebook companion and the project page; each answer with its confidence, the answerer, the evidence and the rule's answer beside it, a disagreement shown, the person's choice a label. Done when the three surfaces give the same answer on the replicas and an override is recorded as a label.
spec: One function answering from a column's state, three surfaces calling it, a project route and page table, and a person's choice recorded as a decision and a label.
plan: Survey the tool registry, the companion, the rules and the evidence.
Write one function and three surfaces over it.
Show the answers beside each column on the Solution page.

decisions.decision: On a project, the rule beside the models is the project's own recorded decision; the bands rule only without one, and named as an approximation.
decisions.why: An answer that contradicts what the project did confuses the person it is meant to help.

decisions.decision: A person's choice is a label when it differs from any answer they were shown.
decisions.why: A choice against a classifier is exactly the label the shadow measurement needs.

decisions.decision: The person's id stays in the label, never in the answer.
decisions.why: The export removes ids from labels; an answer would carry it out of the workspace.

decisions.decision: The companion reads only an existing workspace's routing.
decisions.why: A read-only question must never create a workspace.

change: dclab_rnd/decide.py (new), tools.py and intern/tools.py (the decide tool), notebook_assist.py (--decide, --home), agentic/pages/ledger.py (POST /api/decide and /api/decide/choose), agentic/routers/projects.py (GET /api/projects/{id}/decisions), the Solution page's table, accounts/guard.py, ledger/shadow.py and routing.py (superseded labels; shown answers measured), dclab_core/answerers.py (dclab-core 0.31.0), the web client; tests/test_decide.py (new), test_agents_runtime.py, test_experience_log.py; the plan, the roadmap, CLAUDE.md.

findings.scenario: A person's second answer on a column superseded the first label, yet the measurement counted both.
findings.cause: Supersession was applied per record, and the replacement lives on another record.
findings.fix: Superseded labels are set aside across all labels in the measurement, the demotion and the comparison library.

findings.defect: Reporting a failed verdict as not judged went unnoticed.
findings.scenario: A planted fault merged fail and not judged and every test passed.
findings.cause: The test relied on local model files, absent where it ran.
findings.fix: A stand-in classifier with a real failed verdict.

findings.defect: The bands rule contradicted the project's recorded decisions and was presented as what DCLab would do.
findings.scenario: It disagreed with the studio's rule on 43 of 255 replica decisions, was right on 2 of 18 planted leaks, and called a date-like time column an identifier.
findings.cause: A rule from bands alone, standing in for rules that read the whole table.
findings.fix: On a project the rule is its recorded decision; without one the bands rule is named an approximation; a date is never an identifier.

findings.defect: A choice against a classifier but with the rule was not a label.
findings.scenario: A person agreeing with the rule against a confident classifier left no label.
findings.cause: Only a difference from DCLab's answer made a label.
findings.fix: A difference from any answer shown makes a label.

findings.defect: Records of a person's choice were invisible to the shadow measurement.
findings.scenario: After four choices the measurement reported no answer and no label for the classifier.
findings.cause: The measurement read shadow answers only; the shown answers were not shadows.
findings.fix: The measurement reads the classifier's answer whatever its source.

findings.defect: A person's id left the workspace in the training export.
findings.scenario: The export held the answerer person:u_alice42.
findings.cause: The person's answer carried the id; the export cleans labels, not answers.
findings.fix: The answer says person; the id stays in the label.

findings.defect: One person's repeated choices each made a label.
findings.scenario: Twenty posts could make twenty labels and demote a routed model.
findings.fix: A person's later answer on a column and point supersedes their earlier label.

findings.defect: A choice without a value, or kept nowhere, reported success.
findings.scenario: A body without a value wrote a label of nothing; with no ledger the route answered as if it had kept it.
findings.fix: A value is required, and a decision not kept is an error.

findings.defect: The surfaces could read different routings, and a question could create a workspace.
findings.scenario: With PostgreSQL configured the companion bound a default folder to a new workspace and answered by the rule while the API used a routed model.
findings.cause: The companion opened whatever folder the settings named.
findings.fix: The companion takes the workspace folder, on PostgreSQL only one already bound; every answer says where its routing came from; a routed point is tested on all three.

findings.defect: A failed sealed verdict was shown as not judged.
findings.scenario: Four classifiers with a failed verdict read fail or not judged.
findings.fix: The verdict is shown as recorded.

findings.defect: The tool took any state and any options, and a broken question crashed the companion.
findings.scenario: Values could reach the traces through a free state; a long or unknown option was echoed; malformed input gave a traceback.
findings.cause: A free schema and no checks.
findings.fix: The tool lists the bands with their values; options must be the point's own; a broken question is an error with exit 2.

findings.defect: Parts of the package were neither built nor said.
findings.scenario: No status line said that the copilot review and the companion's cell analysis do not ask on their own.
findings.fix: The status says what is built and what is open; the project page shows the decisions beside each column.

measurements.name: the same question through three surfaces
measurements.gate: on the replicas, each technical point asked through the API, the MCP tool and the companion gives the same answer with its confidence and evidence
measurements.result: 4 columns of the binary replica times 6 technical points: 24 answers identical across the three surfaces, also with a point routed to act
limits: The classifiers' confidence is shown where the fitted models are on the machine.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each planted fault fails a test
measurements.result: 17 of 17 planted faults caught after the tests were strengthened

outcome: A data scientist asks DCLab about a column through the API, an MCP tool or the companion and gets the same answer, with the rule, the classifiers' confidence, the disagreements and the evidence; on a project the rule is the project's own; a person's choice becomes a label.
lessons: Beside a model, show the rule the person's project actually used, not an approximation of it.
A supersession that spans records must be applied across all labels, not per record.
A read-only question must never create state, not even a workspace row.
risks: The copilot review and the companion's cell analysis do not ask on their own yet.
The bands rule is an approximation where there is no project.
